correctness.rationale: The nine rational Hermitian points form a transverse (3,3) complete intersection with G=X(Y²+YZ+Z²). Cayley–Bacharach forces a cubic through eight of them through all nine, while the non-H members of the cubic pencil factor into rational lines. The displayed C0 is smooth and meets H at exactly seven rational points. Exact full-coefficient and seven-constraint-nullspace enumerations establish 180 extremizers, five per omitted pair, with a 72/108 split. High rational point counts and absence of a rational line factor force geometric smoothness; Bezout, absence of degree-two Hermitian closed points and tangent gradients give the claimed contact divisors.

originality.rationale: Beelen–Datta–Montanucci–Niemann establish nonexistence of full nine-point integral intersections for (q,d)=(2,3), not the seven-point optimum or complete 180/72/108 classification; their displayed q=2 pencil specialization is reducible. Homma classifies cubic curves with nine rational points up to projective equivalence, not incidence against a fixed Hermitian cubic. Kaplan–Matei count all ordered cubic pairs by number of rational intersection points, not the conditional smooth-companion census for fixed H. Classical Cayley–Bacharach is credited as prior art. Earlier isolated numerical tables remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed F4 code enumeration or finite geometry table could contain the same exact 180 and contact-count formulas.
